The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, December 1, 1933

Rowdies Here Attack
Office Of Society Said
Backing Fukien Rebels

Hammers Shatter Show Cases Of Shenchow
Kuokwang Publishing Concern Owned
By Revolting General

Clash Looms On Chekiang Border

The Shenchow Kuokwang Publishing Society, alleged Socialist
Democratic propaganda organ under General Chen Ming-shu,
independence leader in Fukien, was made a target of attack by
local rowdies, believed to be elements of Fascist organizations,
at 7 o'clock last night.
A youth, clad in long gown, entered the bookstore at 136
Honan Road, pretending to be a customer, according to the shop-
assistants today. When he reached the counter, he gave a signal,
promptly responded to by three rowdies. They started wrecking
the premises, shattering the show
cases with hammers and escaped
before the arrival of police officers.
Police Arrest Youth
A Chinese policeman, however,
accosted a youth clad in long gown
at corner of Honan and Siking
Roads. He was bleeding and it was
alleged that he was the man who
first entered the bookstore. It also
was said that his head was cut by
flying glass while hammering a
show case.
Taken to the station, the youth
emphatically denied the charge,
adding that he received in the in-
jury accidentally as a piece of glass
fell on his forehead. He was dis-
missed at the police station as no
incriminating evidence could be
found against him.
It is understood that no alarm
was raised by the shop-assistants
during or after the attack.

Attack on propaganda organ of Social Democratic
Party - book shop smashed

At 7 p.m. November 30, four Chinese entered the
Shun Chow Kuo Kwan; Zoe, a Book Shop at 136 Honan Road,
and after cutting the telephone wire smashed a show
window and cupboard. The miscreants subsequently
departed leaving behind paper slips bearing anti-Communist
and pro-Chiang Kai-shek slogans. A male Chinese who was
in the shop at the time was suspected of being one of the
trouble makers and was arrested by the police but subse-
quently released for lack of evidence against him.

This book shop is suspected of being a propaganda
organ of the Social Democratic Party of which General
Chen Ling-chu (陳銘樞) one of the principal promoters
of the Fukien Incident, is the leader.

Made by and Forwarded by D. S. I. Duncan.

With reference to attached reports dated November 20
and December 15 made by D.S. Pitts on the above subject,
diligent enquiries have been kept up by the staff of S.1
but nothing definite can be ascertained regarding the
so-called "上海電影界剋共團 Shanghai Cinema Circles Communist Extermination
Association" or the persons responsible for the attacks
on the bookstores.
While it is reasonable to believe that ex-graduates
of the Whampoa Military Academy who may be members of the
"Blue Shirts Society", engineered the attacks on the Nee
Hwa Motion Picture Studio and the Liang Yue Bookstore,
no proof of this has been forthcoming and it is more likely
that a few irresponsible students with ultra-patriotic ideas
were the guilty parties.
Such an Association as above mentioned, being
of an anti-Communist character would undoubtedly have at
least the moral support of local Government officials.
Nothing further has been heard of the Association since the
attack on the Shun Chow Kuo Kwang Dzoe (神州國光社) Bookstore,
136 Honan Road, on November 30 and it appears as if its
activities have come to an end.

In compliance with the instructions of the Officer i/c
Special Branch regarding offences which have recently been
perpetrated against radical newspapers and bookstores, I have
to report that careful enquiries reveal the following information.
Two attacks only have been made on bookstores which might
be classed as radical in a very modified degree, whilst a third
assault was perpetrated against premises housing a communistic
publication's printing plant.
The first incident occurred at 12.5 p.m. November 12, 1933
at the Liang Yue (良友) Bookstore, No. 851 North Szechuen
Road when the plate-glass show-window of the shop was smashed by
some person or persons unknown, who employed an iron hammer-head
as the means of destruction.
The Liang Yue Bookstore is a Cantonese concern which was
established some seven or eight years ago. The general publi-
cations of this company are of a pictorial nature whilst books
in the new Chinese literary style and topical talking films'
song sheets form the bulk of the sales. The manager of this
firm is one named Wu Lien-teh (伍連德), a graduate of the
Lin Nan (南) University, Canton; he originally joined
the Commercial Press as a draughtsman and held that position
until he established the Liang Yue Bookstore.
On November 15, the above mentioned company received a threat-
ening letter, a translation of which is attached, dated November
13, 1933 from an organisation styling itself "Shanghai Cinema
Circles Communist Extermination Association." This communicat-
ion warned the bookstore not to print or publish any literature
of a radical or reactionary nature and instructed the management
to refrain from offering for sale books written by various "red"

The second incident was seen in the entry by persons unknown

The Shun Chow Quo Kwang Toe was established in 1929 by five Chinese, prominent among whom was General Chen Ming-chu (陳銘樞) who subscribed 60% of the total capital amounting to $380,000 necessary to float the company, which is suspected of being a propaganda organ of the Social Democratic Party of which Chen Ming-chu, one of the principal Promoters of the Fukien Secessionist Movement, is the leader. This was brought about by the fact that when the company was under the management of Tseng Hsien Sung (曾聲) an intimate friend of Chen Ming-chu, Wong Li Shih (王礼錫) one of the most prominent members of the Anti-Bolshevik Group joined the Bookstore through the recommendation of Deu Sih Ban (段錫朋), Vice Minister of Education. Shortly after Wong became Chief Editor of the Bookstore in 1930 he succeeded in effecting a compromise with the Elimination Clique of the Communist Party, of which the aged Chen Tu Siu (陳獨秀), now undergoing a term of imprisonment, was the Chief. By this compromise members of the Elimination Clique agreed to cooperate with the Anti-Bolshevik Group in launching a propaganda campaign hostile to the Stalin Clique as well as other political organisations not seeing eye-to-eye with their doctrines.

Consequently the greater part of the literature published by the bookstore is compiled by either members of the Anti-Bolshevik Group or by those of the Elimination Clique, with the object of furthering their views to the embarrassment of the Nationalist Government.

Subject (in full) Enquiry regarding offences which have recently been perpetrated against bookstores, newspapers, etc. supporting the Kuomintang.

Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by A.G. [Signature]

The only instance which has come to the notice of the Municipal Police of an offence perpetrated against bookstores strongly supporting the Kuomintang is that in which an attack was made on the Hsin Kwang (新光) Bookstore, No. 88 Burkill Road at 3.30 p.m. November 13, 1933 by six young Chinese males of the student class. Full details of this outrage are as follows:

The Hsin Kwang Bookstore has for more than a year acted as the general distribution agent for the "Social News" (社会新闻), a bi-weekly mosquito publication which devotes its pages to the exposing of reactionary elements and to advocating national unity. It is definitely of an anti-communist nature and attempts to show its readers the fallacies and drawbacks of the "red" doctrine. Although only a mosquito paper it enjoys a fairly large circulation and is well received locally. The paper has its editorial and printing offices at the Social News Agency at premises located next to the Headquarters of the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang, West Gate, Nantao, its editor being one Ting Muh Tsung (丁默村), a reformed communist. Although it has not been definitely ascertained, it is believed that this publication is subsidized by the local Kuomintang authorities so that the latter's views on the failings of radicalism may be broadcast.

At 3.30 p.m. November 13, two young Chinese males of the student type entered the front door of the Hsin Kwang Bookstore and stated that they wished to subscribe to the Social News. One of these individuals gave his name as Wong Ts Dee (王志田) and declared that he was a student at the Great China University, off Kiaochow Road, O.O.L. Almost immediately afterwards

The Nyi Woo Company was smashed.

Recently a new film company was established called

if they don't change their attitude in future, more vigorous
action will be taken. It is also learned that they also
smashed the Liang Yue Book Store and Kwong Hwa book company
as these two establishments are also communistic organs.

"Union of the people for the suppression of Communists."

The Liang Yue bookshop is closed on Sunday, and there is only one shop assistant left in charge of the premises, the master Woo Liang Dah (伍聯德), and the other assistants, living out. The assistant does not know where his master lives, except that he thinks it is on Yuen Yuen Road. He does not know whether his master is interested in any political party, but stated that there were some Russian books, translated into Chinese; on sale at the shop.
D.S.Moore of the Political Branch was informed of the occurrence.
